pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis (secondary to an Ovarian Teratoma) THE SMOKING GUN: Pelvic ultrasonography/MRI revealing a hidden mature cystic teratoma (ovarian dermoid cyst) containing ectopic neural tissue, alongside the characteristic 'extreme delta brush' pattern on EEG. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: This paraneoplastic auto-immune condition is triggered when ectopic neural tissue within an ovarian teratoma presents GluN1 subunits of the N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor to the systemic immune system. The body generates cross-reactive IgG antibodies against these extracellular subunits. These antibodies cause cross-linking and internalization of NMDA receptors on GABAergic interneurons in the brain, leading to a profound loss of inhibitory pathways. The resulting hyperglutamatergic state drives the characteristic sequence of symptoms: early psychiatric disturbance, followed by dyskinesias, catatonia, severe autonomic breakdown, and central hypoventilation. Treatment requires prompt surgical resection of the teratoma alongside aggressive immunosuppression (plasma exchange, IVIG, and monoclonal antibodies).
